title: Ministry of Finance Intelligent RAG
summary: An Arabic-first retrieval and question-answering system for government documents, from scanned pages to evaluated evidence.
problem: A question could depend on a scanned circular, a digital PDF or passages in multiple documents. Corrupted text and incomplete retrieval made it hard to give grounded answers.
role: Worked on ingestion quality, Arabic OCR fallback, retrieval and reranking evaluation, production question analysis, and PostgreSQL and object storage integration. Prototyped knowledge graph extraction and entity resolution.
challenges: Separate bad OCR and missing pages from search failures. Retrieved passages can be individually relevant while missing evidence needed across sources.
decision: Keep OCR fallback conditional on extraction quality. Evaluate retrieval and citing behavior independently, and test graph enrichment as an experiment with a separate baseline.
evaluation: Used two benchmark sets of 25 and 22 questions to track Recall@K, mean reciprocal rank, full evidence hits and multi-source hits. Separately reviewed whether answers cited files or pages and handled out-of-corpus questions.
outcome: Benchmark B measured 87.1% mean Recall@K and 0.786 MRR across 22 questions. The two sets contain different questions and should be read as separate evaluations.
lesson: A high ranking score can coexist with weak citations. An answer-level audit identifies gaps that aggregate retrieval metrics miss.
next: Grow the multi-source benchmark and add citation-level checks against a wider range of scanned Arabic documents.

stages.name: Sources
stages.detail: Collect digital and scanned PDFs with source metadata from object storage and PostgreSQL.

stages.name: Ingest & OCR
stages.detail: Extract text per page. Route pages with weak text quality to Arabic OCR and retain page metadata.

stages.name: Index
stages.detail: Segment the text into passages and index embeddings with document and page references.

stages.name: Retrieve
stages.detail: Match questions to candidate passages using semantic similarity.

stages.name: Rerank
stages.detail: Reorder retrieved passages for relevance before building context.

stages.name: Answer
stages.detail: Generate a grounded answer and evaluate evidence coverage and citation behavior.

title: Intelligent Customer Support Chatbot
summary: A conversational support system for the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company with session context and agent escalation.
problem: Support interactions need context across messages, an option to escalate and enough operational visibility to diagnose failed requests.
role: Worked with FastAPI, Rasa, MongoDB and Rancher deployments. Investigated deployment issues, analyzed conversation histories and worked on per-user session context and live-agent fallback.
challenges: Tie application failures to deployment state and conversation behavior. Preserve a conversation’s context through automated routing and escalation.
decision: Treat user sessions as independent state and trace messages across the API, conversational engine and action layer.
evaluation: Reviewed conversation records and deployment diagnostics to identify interaction patterns and operational failures.
outcome: Analyzed exported conversation histories and investigated deployment failures on the running Kubernetes stack. Public service-level figures are unavailable.
lesson: Session continuity needs attention at component boundaries, particularly when an interaction changes ownership.
next: Add end-to-end checks for concurrent conversations, fallback and handoff behavior.

stages.name: Visitor
stages.detail: A visitor submits a message with a conversation identifier.

stages.name: API
stages.detail: FastAPI receives the message and routes the request with session context.

stages.name: Conversation
stages.detail: Rasa interprets the request and selects a response or custom action.

stages.name: State & actions
stages.detail: Actions run business logic, while MongoDB supports conversation history and analysis.

stages.name: Reply or handoff
stages.detail: Return a response or route the visitor to an agent when human assistance is needed.

title: Electronic Know Your Customer Platform
summary: A modular verification workflow for identity documents, face matching and liveness, with asynchronous execution and observability.
problem: A verification flow spans long-running processing, sensitive submissions and a case review interface, so failure and completion must be visible across services.
role: Implemented session and customer validation, face cropping and object storage integration, configurable workflows and interfaces for capture and review. Instrumented service dependencies and built operational dashboards.
challenges: Maintain a traceable job across APIs and processing services. Give operators diagnostic context while masking sensitive values.
decision: Represent verification as a job with queryable state. Use queue boundaries for slow work and attach correlation context to service logs and metrics.
evaluation: Inspect session states, processing failures and dependency measurements in operational dashboards. Public biometric accuracy figures are unavailable.
outcome: Added Prometheus instrumentation across HTTP, database, Redis, gRPC, object storage and queues, with Grafana dashboards and correlated audit logs.
lesson: A stage-level status map is as important to operations as the final verification result.
next: Extend consistency checks for retries and validate accessibility across capture and review screens.

stages.name: Submission
stages.detail: An authenticated session submits identity images and capture metadata.

stages.name: OCR
stages.detail: Extract and validate identity document fields.

stages.name: Face match
stages.detail: Compare the document portrait with face capture.

stages.name: Liveness
stages.detail: Evaluate the live capture and return verification signals.

stages.name: Review
stages.detail: Record the outcome and expose stage-level jobs and metrics for authorized operators.

title: Modern Data Platform & Lakehouse
summary: A data platform prototype exploring batch ingestion, CDC and analytics-ready data through the Bronze, Silver and Gold layers.
problem: A platform must ingest source changes, support repeatable transforms and deliver trustworthy analytics without operational complexity that the workload does not justify.
role: Prototyped PostgreSQL batch and CDC ingestion, Airflow orchestration, dbt transformations, and data validation. Compared warehouse and lakehouse architecture choices.
challenges: Keep snapshots and CDC events aligned. Check transformation outputs and failure recovery through the batch and streaming paths.
decision: Preserve raw data before applying contracts and business models. Compare warehouse and lakehouse options with the same validation questions.
evaluation: Exercised pipeline stages and dbt checks on project data. Investigated configuration and orchestration errors during testing.
outcome: Implemented batch and CDC pipeline prototypes using PostgreSQL, Airflow, Kafka and Debezium, with dbt models and S3-compatible SeaweedFS storage. Apache Iceberg catalog choices were researched.
lesson: The storage format, orchestration and consumption layers have different responsibilities. Model them separately when comparing architectures.
next: Test replay and schema evolution, and compare an Iceberg-backed path against the warehouse baseline.

stages.name: PostgreSQL
stages.detail: Start with a source database and a defined snapshot boundary.

stages.name: Batch & CDC
stages.detail: Orchestrate batches with Airflow and capture database changes through Debezium and Kafka.

stages.name: Bronze
stages.detail: Retain source records and change events in a raw layer.

stages.name: Silver
stages.detail: Clean, reconcile and validate source data through transformations.

stages.name: Gold
stages.detail: Expose modeled facts and metrics for consumption.

title: AI Research & Experimental Systems
summary: Experiments with graph extraction, Arabic NLP, embedding retrieval and local model serving.
problem: Model quality, hardware limits and downstream use vary enough to require small controlled experiments.
role: Prototyped multilingual entity and relation extraction, entity resolution and Neo4j graph ingestion. Compared multilingual embeddings and reranking. Tested quantized models behind a local inference API.
challenges: Arabic text normalization, ambiguous entity links and accelerator memory can affect results in different ways.
decision: Use a small benchmark and track individual errors before integrating a model. Keep graph personalization as an exploration until there is a clear evaluation baseline.
evaluation: Compared retrieval rankings and false matches, inspected entity extraction output and tried CPU fallback when GPU memory was insufficient.
outcome: Built a graph ingestion proof of concept and exercised local LLM serving and multilingual retrieval configurations.
lesson: Configuration changes are easier to interpret when the data, candidate set and evaluation labels are frozen.
next: Define a reproducible personalization benchmark and expand local serving measurements across hardware.

stages.name: Corpus
stages.detail: Choose bilingual examples and establish evaluation labels.

stages.name: Extract
stages.detail: Identify entities and relations, then resolve duplicate mentions.

stages.name: Compare
stages.detail: Compare graph, retrieval and local inference configurations against a baseline.

stages.name: Record
stages.detail: Review failure examples and record limits and follow-up questions.
